g.text: Figure 5a Sequence Diagram — PLN-04 Assertion-level Risk Reasoning (P1)
From the A1 node dispatch to the human decision at Gate_P1_step1: four-layer context assembly, LLM call,
structured output, four-level validation, StatePatch merge
Agents never call each other (5.3). A1 hands over
EngagementState; A4 returns a StatePatch. A1 itself
never calls the LLM (4.1), and neither do A5 and A9.
This figure follows PLN-04 only. PLN-01, PLN-16, PLN-18 and
the other P1 procedures of A4 take the same path; PLN-01
supplies the proposed materiality shown at the gate below.
Rules enumerate material accounts x standard assertions plus
disclosure items, so omission cannot occur by construction (P1).
Revenue Occurrence and Cutoff carry fraudRelated = true and
level = significant; these are preset and read-only for the
LLM (ASA240-P27), which only rates and proposes additions.
Per-objective reasoning — one LLM call per procedure execution
1 System role, output JSON schema, 8.3 constraints (fixed template)
2 Standards fragment text verbatim; pointers must cite fragment ids
3 Task prompt template + params + this objective and its RiskItem
4 Data rows and columns from inputs, prior_risk_register summary
EngagementState itself never enters the prompt (8.5, 18.5).
temperature = 0 lowers variance, it is no guarantee.
[no valid pointer, or semantic check fails (8.6 levels 3-4)]
Engine fallback: ProcedureRun failed, ReviewTask kind failed, no Judgment - Figure 5b
Scope: this break belongs to the per-objective loop, not to the
validation loop above it. Only exhausted format retries end the
execution here; the other three branches fall through to buildJudgment.
c_ev 0.3 and c_llm 0.2 apply. c_rule is hybrid-only and
c_critic needs A7, which an L2 procedure does not use, so
both weights fall to zero and the rest are renormalised (8.4).
Confidence is never taken from the LLM on its own.
JudgmentEngine only builds the Judgment and returns it; it writes no
business Store. A4 carries the Judgments in its StatePatch and A1
writes them after mergePatch (18.5). The AuditTrail write stays immediate.
Nothing in the patch is in a business Store yet. The instance writes
only the AuditTrail itself; every business result below is written by
A1 once the patch has passed the four checks (18.4, 18.5).
Business Store first, checkpoint second (18.5). A checkpoint
restores execution; it is not the audit trail behind M-07.
The re-run that succeeds joins this same commit point.
Execution marked failed, ReviewTask kind failed; the gate is not reached - Figure 5b
Scope: this break sits at the top level of the figure, outside the
mergePatch loop. It ends the sequence - the gate below is never entered.
[until an approve with a current targetVersion is written]
[level changed, or revenue fraud presumption lowered]
A10 transcribes the structured fields; no LLM sits in the write
path (18.5). One GateDecision per gate: targetId is the
risk_register snapshot, per-item changes travel as edits[].
[d.decision = approve, version and gate state valid]
Only the approve branch leaves this loop. Stale, insufficient_info and
reject all re-present the current version at the same gate, so nothing
below is reached without an approval bound to a current version (18.5).
Objective-level pack assembly, coverage gate, AuditPlan vN
and the PLN-15 narrative, then Gate_P1_step2 — see Figure 4a
Store or trail behind a contract interface
Exit of the fragment it is drawn in, nothing below it runs
A1 passes EngagementState, A4 returns StatePatch (5.3)
Reads via StateQuery, writes via DecisionSubmit (18.2)
Business results are written by A1 after mergePatch
Only an approve leaves the gate
Stale, insufficient_info and reject re-present the current version (18.5)
One execution of one procedure is one call (8.5)
Prompt, model version, hashes, tokens, validation (M-07)
